note: Every Live series card of MLB The Show 19 (the roster of each MLB club at the edition's last roster update) as ShowZone keeps it, as [uuid, name, team, position, secondary positions, overall, born]. "born" is a US state or a country, "" where ShowZone names none (4 cards). Written by npm run import:mlb-showzone from ShowZone's cached answers; read by npm run build:mlb-seasons.

source.name: MLB The Show 19 Live series
source.provenance: Sony's own API for this edition is gone. ShowZone (showzone.gg), a fan-run card database that is not the publisher, keeps every Live card of the edition at its last roster update and serves them from a public data API (data.showzone.gg), read once on 2026-11-08: 74 pages of 100 cards, MLB The Show 18 to 21. showzone.gg's robots.txt disallows /api on its own host; the data host serves no robots.txt. ShowZone states 'All Rights Reserved' and publishes no terms; as with Sony's own data, the rights are not cleared. Its MLB The Show 21 equals Sony's own API (scripts/data/mlb-the-show-21.json) on all 2,092 cards, uuid, name, team, position, overall and birthplace, though ShowZone keeps no secondary positions for that edition; its team ids are named by that edition's codes and teams, which the clubs kept from 2018 to 2021. Checked against Sony's own pages in the Wayback Machine: ShowZone holds the new overall and the team of 142 of the 143 changes of the last roster update (September 27, 2019); the other is Giovanny Gallegos (Cardinals, 82), the one Live card ShowZone lacks. The 10 Live cards whose page was captured agree on overall, secondary positions and birthplace.
